title: Adaptive epochal KV resharding and scheduler fairness overhaul
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements an epochal (versioned) approach to KV shard reshaping and a concurrent scheduler fairness layer to reduce long-tail latency and hotspots during bursts. Instead of monolithic shard migrations or full-stop rebalances, we introduce epoch markers, a background migration agent that performs incremental, rate-limited data movement, and a scheduler token-bucket that enforces bounded fairness across sessions and tenants.

Motivation:
- Persistent hotkeys and uneven shard density cause transient latency spikes during rolling upgrades and model swaps.
- Current prefetch/eviction paths and scheduler heuristics interact poorly under mixed short/long session workloads, causing starvation for small interactive requests.
- Dependency drift: updated RocksDB bindings and the allocator library (jemalloc->mimalloc) enable more compact compaction options but require migration support.

Goals & acceptance criteria:
- Implement epoched shard metadata so a shard resize or rekey produces a new epoch without blocking serving paths.
- Background migration agent moves slot ranges incremental and supports backpressure signals from the scheduler.
- Scheduler fairness: introduce per-session soft-quotas (tokens) with refill rates derived from request cost histograms; ensure small requests see <=10% p99 improvement in tail latency.
- Migration must be cancelable and pauseable; fallback policy to preserve correctness on partial moves.
- End-to-end tests and load tests showing no increase in median latency and <5% tail regressions during migrations.

Design overview:
1) Epoch metadata: add an epoch field to KV shard descriptors; all new writes are tagged with current epoch. Reads consult epoch hints; if a read spans epochs we use the migration agent to route or materialize a consistent view.
2) Migration agent: single control-plane task per node that uses cooperative yielding; moves keys in range-based windows (configurable window_size and rate). Agent emits progress and can use adaptive windows when load is high.
3) Scheduler fairness: token-bucket per-session with cost estimates (tokens per tokenized input). Short sessions get priority by having lower token costs; long-running sessions can borrow with probabilistic backoff.
4) Dependency upgrades: bump RocksDB to 7.9 and switch allocator to mimalloc v2.1 in a controlled canary; include compatibility shim for our compacted SST layout.
5) GC & compaction coordination: migration agent notifies compactor to avoid deleting source SSTs until migration epoch committed.

Migration & rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary): feature-flag epoch metadata and scheduler token-buckets on 5% of runtime hosts; run synthetic traffic (small interactive + long batch) for 72 hours. Validate metrics.
- Phase 1 (gradual): increment canary percentage and enable background migration agent in read-only dry-run mode to collect timing profiles.
- Phase 2 (enabled): start incremental migration for low-traffic tenants with tight backpressure thresholds.
- Phase 3 (full): enable across cluster, coordinate RocksDB and allocator upgrade during low-traffic window.
- Rollback: disable agent and revert epoch pointer to previous stable epoch; fall back to existing eviction semantics.

Observability & metrics:
- New metrics: kv.migration.bytes_moved, kv.migration.progress_pct, kv.epoch.active_epochs, scheduler.tokens.used, scheduler.tokens.refill_rate, scheduler.fairness.rejections.
- Dashboards: release a migration overview dashboard (link below) and an SLO comparison dashboard to track p50/p95/p99 before/after migrations.
- Alerts: trigger if migration rate drops >50% under normal load or if p99 increases >20% for 15m.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for epoch descriptor logic and read/write path branching.
- Integration tests simulating cross-epoch reads and partial migration failures.
- Chaos tests: leader preemption, network partition, and agent restart.
- Performance tests: reproduce mixed workload at 2x production QPS and validate tail latency improvements.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: partial migrations could create inconsistent reads. Mitigation: read-path retains ability to consult both epochs until migration committed; migration uses two-phase commit style markers.
- Risk: scheduler token-buckets could throttle critical background work. Mitigation: background tasks are on a separate priority lane with adjustable token ceilings.
- Risk: dependency upgrade regressions. Mitigation: keep canary binary with old bindings; automated diff on compaction outputs.

Acceptance checklist:
- [ ] Epoch field persisted in shard metadata and accepted by read/write paths.
- [ ] Migration agent implemented, feature-flagged, and dry-run tested.
- [ ] Scheduler token-bucket primitives added and validated under load.
- [ ] RocksDB and mimalloc upgrades validated in canary.
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts defined and wired to oncall.
- [ ] PRs merged and migration runbook documented in Confluence.
